newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU urges Zambia to resolve election row peacefully.
newsitem.headline: EU urges Zambia to resolve election row peacefully.

text.p: The European Union said on Thursday it regretted Monday's elections in Zambia were not held on a basis acceptable to all parties and urged the government and its opponents to resolve their differences peacefully.

A statement issued by EU president Ireland on behalf of the 15-nation bloc said the EU was "concerned that the absence of political consensus might result in a further decline in the previous standards of governance in Zambia".

Zambia's presidential and parliamentary elections returned President Frederick Chiluba to power for a second term by a landslide but his only serious opponent, Kenneth Kaunda, was barred from standing by a new law.
Some opposition parties said the election was rigged and they would not recognise the result.
The EU urged all parties to avoid confrontation and engage in dialogue to resolve their differences peacefully. It noted that the elections had been held in a peaceful and orderly manner.
"Over the past five years the European Union and member states have taken a major stake in supporting the Zambian government's economic and political reform programme," it said.
"The European Union looks to the Zambian government to reinvigorate the political and economic reform programme."
